SK hynix Becomes Kioxia’s Largest Shareholder

SK hynix has become the largest shareholder of Kioxia, Japan’s largest NAND flash manufacturer.

According to the Nikkei on August 10, Kioxia disclosed that its largest shareholder had changed from Toshiba to the special-purpose company BCPE Pangea Cayman2, or SPC2. SPC2 is the entity through which SK hynix invested via convertible bonds (CBs).

Toshiba previously held a 15.10% stake in Kioxia. However, through seven separate sales conducted between July 15 and August 3, it reduced its stake to 14.06%.

Toshiba previously held a 15.10% stake in Kioxia. However, through seven separate sales conducted between July 15 and August 3, it reduced its stake to 14.06%.

As a result, SPC2, which holds a 14.19% stake in Kioxia, has become the company’s largest shareholder.

SK hynix invested approximately KRW 4 trillion in Kioxia through two SPCs in 2018. SPC1, which was jointly funded by SK hynix, Bain Capital, and other investors, sold its entire stake in June as Bain Capital exited its investment.

SK hynix, meanwhile, has continued to hold SPC2, in which it invested approximately KRW 1.3 trillion. If the convertible bonds are converted into shares, SK hynix could become a voting shareholder of Kioxia.

As a result, SPC2, which holds a 14.19% stake in Kioxia, has become the company’s largest shareholder.

Kioxia is Japan’s largest NAND flash manufacturer. It currently ranks third in the global NAND market, behind Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.

However, SK hynix is currently considered unlikely to exert direct influence over Kioxia’s management. To obtain voting rights, SK hynix would need approvals under competition and antitrust laws in multiple jurisdictions. The Japanese government is also unlikely to grant such approval, given its interest in protecting the country’s domestic semiconductor supply chain.

According to Taiwanese media reports, AI demand has set off a race to raise prices and a scramble for volume in MLCCs.

Word in the industry is that some customers are offering two to three times the going price to major passive component makers such as Yageo (2327) and Murata Manufacturing just to lock down enough supply.

Yageo, for its part, acknowledged that "MLCC demand really is very strong."

Another notable shift is customers racing to lock in long term contracts.

Yageo said AI related customers are increasingly moving to secure passive component supply for the next six months, and in some cases several years out, through long term contracts in order to reduce supply chain risk.

Shipments of high specification applications such as AI servers and data centers are ramping quickly, so demand for high capacity, high reliability products is surging. Large customers generally receive higher priority in capacity allocation, while the volumes available to small and midsize customers keep shrinking. Customers with thin inventories of their own, worried that a component shortfall will disrupt shipments of their finished products, have little choice but to bid higher to secure the limited supply on offer.

Another day, another urge to to pound my chest on $SONY.

The world's #1 chipmaker is officially handing $SONY a $6B fab to make chips for robots.

Today, Nikkei reports $SONY and $TSM are putting ¥1 trillion ($6.3B) behind the image sensor JV they announced in May, moving from MOU to official deal.

Around a quarter of Sony's operating profit comes from image sensing chips. It's the fastest growing profit engine in the company, with operating income up 37% to a record last year, and Sony holds roughly 50% of the global market for this specific type of chip.

These chips are critical for physical AI because a robot has to see the world before it can act in it. Compute is crowded and actuators are commoditizing, but nothing moves until the machine perceives, and perception starts at the sensor. Every humanoid, autonomous vehicle, and drone needs eyes before it needs a brain.

This stacks on top of a second deal $SONY just inked. 

Three weeks ago they signed the definitive agreement with Mitsubishi Electric on a JV that puts Sony sensors with AI baked onto the chip directly into factory floors, launching in October. Mitsubishi gets Sony's eyes into the factories that exist today while TSMC builds capacity for the machines that don't exist yet.

That's massive physical AI upside sitting inside a cheap stock the market forgot about, at well under 20x forward.

So before you look at overvalued high beta robotics names, just know $SONY's role in this revolution.

基础设施层的预算池最清晰。 NVIDIA在生命科学资料中引用全球制药研发支出约3,000亿美元/年。若AI计算、数据工程、模拟和软件最终占研发预算1%—3%，仅制药行业就对应约30亿—90亿美元的年度数字科学预算；这还没有计算材料、化工、半导体、能源、气候和工程设计。

存储下一个买盘似乎出现苗头了

存储现在不缺抄底资金，缺的是持续性买盘。

每次三星、海力士、美光大跌，都会有人接。但这些资金很多是短线抄底、空头回补，能拉出一两天反弹，却很难推动一轮稳定行情。

问题还是出在波动率。

现在韩国股市波动率太高，而三星和海力士又占了KOSPI很大权重。机构一旦要降低风险，最直接的做法就是先减掉这些高波动、高弹性、流动性又好的仓位。

所以高波动率对存储有两层影响。

第一，新资金不敢持续买。
第二，已经在场内的资金，也会优先减仓。

这也是为什么存储的基本面可能没变，股价却依然很脆弱。市场一旦进入risk off，资金未必会先卖基本面最差的公司，而是先卖最能降低组合波动率的资产。

相比微软、谷歌、亚马逊这类现金流更稳定的大科技，存储的周期属性更强，对产品价格、供需、库存和CapEx都更敏感。

当市场愿意承担风险时，存储弹性最大。
当市场开始收缩风险时，存储也最容易先被卖。

所以我现在更关注的，不是下一次谁来抄底，而是谁愿意连续买。

真正有效的信号有几个：

1. VKOSPI开始持续下降；
2. 三星和海力士的单日波动明显收窄；
3. 外资不再只是单日巨额流入，而是连续多个交易日净买入；
4. 下一次市场调整时，存储不再成为跌幅最大的方向。

当这些条件出现，说明市场开始重新接受存储的风险，机构也重新获得了配置能力。

所以，存储的下一个买盘，不在下一次暴跌里。

它会出现在韩国市场波动率下降之后，持续性资金重新回来，而且市场下跌时，存储不再被优先卖出的那一刻。

Policy support is real. It doesn’t make any of these automatically cheap.

Check the price before you check the narrative.

GLW. Corning.

Less obvious, but Corning owns a majority stake in Hemlock Semiconductor, one of the few US polysilicon producers.

Domestic content requirements move upstream. Somebody has to make the material, and there are not many American options.

FSLR. First Solar.

The largest US solar manufacturer, and the only one at scale using cadmium telluride thin film instead of Chinese crystalline silicon.

Their whole manufacturing base is already domestic. The rules were essentially written around what they already do.

TE. T1 Energy, formerly Freyr Battery.

A US solar and battery manufacturing platform building modules and cells domestically rather than importing them.

The new incentives are built around fully domestic supply chains, which is the entire thesis of this company.
